description:
**SUPERSEDED 2026-05-10** by the reference-impl extraction epic (see related link). The work this bead identified — adding integration tests to calendars-server, contacts-server, tasks-server — is now happening as children .5, .6, .7 of that epic, as a side-effect of writing public feature-gated reference implementations.

Original text below for history:

---

Empty/missing tests/ on:
- crate-jmap-calendars-server/ (no tests/ files)
- crate-jmap-contacts-server/ (no tests/ files)
- crate-jmap-tasks-server/ (no tests/ files)

Peer server crates have integration tests:
- jmap-mail-server: 4 tests
- jmap-sharing-server: 4 tests
- jmap-chat-server: 1 test
- jmap-filenode-server: 1 test

Either tests are missing (and these crates aren't ready to publish) or the test discipline is genuinely asymmetric. Calendars/Contacts/Tasks are also the three crates where the README claims of method counts have drifted (calendars: 19 vs 20; contacts: nonexistent jscontact module). Likely correlated.

Fix: add wiremock-based integration tests at parity with the other server crates. Even a smoke test ("register handlers, dispatch one method, validate response shape") is better than nothing.

---

**Why superseded:** investigating this bead surfaced that the 4 already-tested server crates carry **5,406 LOC of in-memory backend implementations buried inside their `tests/common/` directories** — one MemoryBackend per JMAP capability, cookie-cut, invisible to docs.rs and external consumers. Executing this bead as-scoped would add another 1,500–9,000 LOC of the same buried pattern to the 3 untested crates.

The reference-impl extraction epic exits the pattern: each server crate gets a public, feature-gated `memory::MemoryBackend` in `src/`; tests use the public impl; the 3 currently-untested crates get reference impls + tests in one pass. This bead's specific work is its children .5, .6, .7.
title: P2: 3 server crates have no integration tests
